prompt_text: Who is the best personal injury lawyer in Miami for a car accident case?
answer_verbatim:
There’s no single objectively “best” personal injury lawyer for every car-accident case — the right attorney depends on your needs (severity of injuries, fault issues, uninsured motorist involvement, language, trial vs. settlement preference, budget). I can help you find a great lawyer in Miami, but here’s a practical way to pick the best one for your situation.

How to choose the best Miami personal injury lawyer for a car accident
- Experience and focus: Look for lawyers who handle car-accident and personal-injury cases routinely (not generalists). Ask how many similar cases they’ve handled and how many went to trial.
- Track record: Ask about significant settlements/verdicts in Miami-Dade and whether they have results for injuries like yours.
- Trial ability: Insurers take trial‑ready lawyers more seriously. Ask whether they try cases themselves or refer them out.
- Reputation and peer recognition: Ratings (Martindale‑Hubbell, Avvo, Super Lawyers), membership in plaintiff organizations (Florida Justice Association), and client reviews matter.
- Communication and team: Who will actually work on the case (attorney vs. paralegal)? How quickly do they return calls/texts? Will you meet the attorney in person?
- Fees and costs: Most PI lawyers work on contingency — commonly about one‑third (30–40%) of recovery, but confirm the exact percentage and whether it changes if suit is filed. Clarify who advances case costs and how medical liens are handled.
- Local knowledge: Miami-Dade experience, familiarity with local courts, judges, and medical providers helps.
- Language/cultural fit: If you need Spanish or Haitian Creole, look for bilingual lawyers.

Questions to ask in a free consultation
- How long have you handled car-accident/personal-injury cases in Miami?
- What percentage of your practice is car-accident work?
- How many cases like mine have you handled? Any outcomes you can share?
- Will you handle my case or a member of your team?
- Do you try cases? How many jury trials in the past 3–5 years?
- How do you charge (contingency percentage, costs, lien handling)?
- What’s your typical timeline and communication frequency?
- Can you provide client references or online reviews?

Where to search and verify
- Florida Bar (search attorney name to check license/discipline)
- Avvo, Martindale‑Hubbell, Super Lawyers, Yelp, Google Reviews
- Florida Justice Association / local plaintiff lawyer groups
- Court records (for trial/verdict searches)

Red flags
- Guarantees of a specific dollar amount or that you’ll win
- No written fee agreement
- Frequent poor reviews mentioning missed deadlines or poor communication
- Pressure to sign immediately or unwillingness to let you compare firms

If you want, I can:
- Provide a short list of Miami attorneys/firms matched to your needs (tell me your ZIP code, severity of injuries, whether language preference matters, and whether the other driver is insured)
- Give a script you can use during consultations

Which would you prefer?
